display.purpose: Page titles and the quest-detail title. One per screen.

body.purpose: Default text for descriptions, lists, form fields.

label.purpose: Section headers and field labels, often uppercase.

micro.purpose: Smallest text — progress counters, footer hints.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Instant-feeling hover/active color swaps on buttons, nav items, chips.

motion.name: progress-fill
motion.purpose: Progress bar fill animating to the new percentage.

motion.name: completion-pop
motion.purpose: Quest Complete banner entrance — completion should feel like an event.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single most important action on a screen (accept quest, save, export).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #fbbf24; color: #0f172a; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 8px; border: none; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #d97706; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #fbbf24; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: #334155; color: #f1f5f9; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 8px; border: none; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #475569; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Low-emphasis action, often paired with an icon (Add, Restore).
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #94a3b8; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 8px; border: none; font-size: 0.75rem; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.15s, background-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: #f1f5f9; background: #334155; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard text field used across quest editing and settings.
components.css: .ds-label { display: block; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; color: #94a3b8; margin-bottom: 4px; } .ds-input { background: #1e293b; color: #f1f5f9; border: 1px solid #475569; border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 12px; font-size: 0.875rem; width: 100%; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #94a3b8; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(251,191,36,0.5); }

components.name: Selected Chip
components.description: Toggle chip for roles, departments, tags — selected state.
components.css: .ds-chip { border-radius: 9999px; padding: 4px 12px; font-size: 0.75rem; border: 1px solid #475569; background: transparent; color: #94a3b8; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.15s; } .ds-chip-selected { border-color: #fbbf24; color: #fbbf24; background: rgba(251,191,36,0.15); }

components.name: Card
components.description: Top-level content container — settings sections, dashboard tiles.
components.html:

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Pill showing a quest's current status (color varies by status).
components.css: .ds-status-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 2px 8px; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; color: white; }

narrative.overview:
VOV reads like a lone explorer's quest log carried into a cave: everything sits in a deep midnight-navy dark (#0f172a), and the only warmth in the room is the single torch-gold accent (#fbbf24) marking what matters right now — the active nav item, the primary action, the objective still glowing at 60% complete. There is no second competing accent color; gold is reserved and precise, the way a torch is the one light source you trust.

Depth is conveyed entirely through three steps of background darkness (surface -> surface-raised -> surface-overlay) rather than shadows — nothing casts light in this world, things simply sit closer to or further from the dark. The interface is calm and utilitarian at rest (this is an Operate surface: task management, not a marketing page) but the interaction layer — button presses, status chip toggles, quest completion — gets a tactile, game-like snap rather than a corporate fade, because the product's whole premise is that admin work should feel a little bit like play.
keyCharacteristics: Single accent color (torch gold), used sparingly — active states, primary actions, progress fills, never decoration
Tonal-only depth: three background steps, zero box-shadow
Dense, utilitarian layout (Operate mode) with playful micro-interactions layered on top
System font stack throughout — no display/brand typeface, personality comes from color and motion, not type

rules.name: The One Torch Rule
rules.body: Torch Gold is the only color allowed to signal "this is active / this is the primary action." If a screen needs to draw attention to two things at once, one of them is wrong, not the palette.

rules.name: The No-Flourish Rule
rules.body: There is no italic, no serif, no display weight above 700. If a moment needs more emphasis, reach for color (gold) or motion (framer-motion), not a heavier or fancier typeface.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats above the page by casting a shadow. If a future component needs to feel "lifted," reach for one more tonal step or a border first; only add a soft shadow as a last resort, and keep it ambient/diffuse.

dos: Do keep Torch Gold reserved for "this is active / this is primary" — one accent, used sparingly (The One Torch Rule).
Do express elevation with the three tonal steps before reaching for a shadow (The Flat-By-Default Rule).
Do use rounded-lg (8px) for anything a user directly interacts with and rounded-xl (12px) for the container one level up.
Do let completion/success moments feel like an event — a spring-scale pop or a colored banner — not a silent state flip.
donts: Don't introduce a second full-opacity accent color for emphasis; desaturate to Fog Slate or use a semantic status color instead.
Don't add box-shadow to cards, modals, or dropdowns as a first instinct — try one more tonal step first.
Don't run Torch Gold at full opacity across a large fill; keep large fills at 15% opacity and let the border/text carry full saturation.
Don't introduce a second typeface or an italic/serif treatment for emphasis (The No-Flourish Rule).
